An electric-potential-augmented benchmark dataset for electrical capacitance tomography: electric-potential supervision for future physics-guided learning
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract While deep learning has significantly advanced image reconstruction of electrical capacitance tomography (ECT), most public datasets retain only capacitance vectors and permittivity distributions and do not expose the excitation-wise electric potential field, a physical intermediate in the forward mapping. To address this, we present an electric-potential-augmented ECT benchmark dataset generated via a COMSOL–MATLAB pipeline for a fixed eight-electrode sensor. The dataset comprises 20 000 randomized samples across four typical flow-pattern families. Alongside conventional capacitance vectors and permittivity images, each sample preserves eight spatially registered full-field potential maps. Governing equations and field-perturbation visualizations characterize the relation between potential and dielectric structure. As an initial use of this physical information, we introduce potential-field intermediate supervision to guide representation learning in simple forward and inverse models. Under sample-disjoint independent and identically distributed (IID) and fully held-out two-bar out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, potential supervision reduces forward capacitance-prediction mean squared error (MSE) by 56.8% and 74.6%, respectively, relative to a structure- and capacity-aligned control. In an exploratory forward experiment, a low-weight partial differential equation residual yields 5.3%–8.3% lower mean potential-prediction MSE. For inverse reconstruction, the simple model reduces mean MSE by 14.3% and 3.0% on IID and OOD data, respectively, relative to the same control. The more modest inverse gains are consistent with the difficulty of recovering dense potential maps from limited capacitance measurements. These results provide initial controlled evidence for the value of potential-field supervision. The dataset and reference experiments together offer a foundation and methodological insights for developing more advanced field-supervised, physics-informed, and data-consistent ECT methods.

nodes.name: CoBiDiff: anatomy-aware bidirectional diffusion for left atrium cross-modal augmentation
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate delineation of the left atrium (LA) from cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) and computed tomography (CT) images plays an important role in atrial fibrillation assessment and treatment planning. However, the limited availability of expert-annotated cardiac datasets restricts the robustness and generalizability of deep learning–based segmentation models, particularly in cross-modal scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose CoBiDiff, a collaborative bidirectional diffusion framework that explicitly incorporates anatomical constraints into unpaired cross-modal cardiac image augmentation. The framework is developed using unpaired CT and MR volumes from the MICCAI 2017 multi-modality whole heart segmentation (MM-WHS) challenge dataset, focusing specifically on the LA region. A shared diffusion backbone is employed to jointly model both imaging modalities, while signed distance functions (SDFs) are incorporated as structural representations to provide anatomical guidance during generation. To reduce the influence of artificial CT field-of-view boundaries, boundary regions are suppressed through noise replacement and gradient smoothing strategies. In addition, a soft spatial extent loss is introduced to maintain anatomically plausible foreground spatial extents during synthesis. An SDF dropout strategy is further introduced during training to strengthen image-conditioned anatomical inference and improve anatomical coherence. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework generates LA images with improved structural consistency across modalities. The proposed method achieved Dice coefficients of 86.53% and 95.04%, and average symmetric surface distances of 1.511 mm and 0.623 mm for CT-to-MR and MR-to-CT augmentation, respectively, on the MM-WHS 2017 dataset. CoBiDiff provides a practical framework for expanding limited cardiac imaging datasets without requiring paired cross-modal images. By combining diffusion-based synthesis with anatomy-aware constraints, CoBiDiff improves the downstream utility of generated samples for cardiac segmentation. The full implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/PencilSC/CoBiDiff to support reproducible and open research.

nodes.name: Observation of the ultra-high-energy $\gamma$-ray emission from theG25.0+0.0 region with LHAASO
nodes.venue: Astronomy & Astrophysics
nodes.abstract: We report the detection of very-high-energy (VHE, 100 GeV < E < 100 TeV) and ultra-high-energy (UHE, E > 100 TeV) ^ emissions from the direction of the star-forming region G25.0+0.0, observed by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). We find that the emission observed by the Water Cherenkov Detector Array (WCDA) is best described by two distinct components, including the extended source J1837EXT with a significance of 50σ and the point-like source J1837PS with a significance of 14σ. In contrast, the 1.3 km 2 array (KM2A) detects only a single component, J1837EXT, at a significance of 30σ. The emission above 100 TeV is resolved into only one point-like source with a significance of 8.3σ, and smooth connections with the spectral energy distribution (SED) of J1837EXT below 100 TeV imply a possible common origin. By combining multiwavelength data, we attribute the emission origin from J1837PS to two pulsar wind nebula (PWN) systems: G25.24 dominates the VHE emission, while AX J1837 contributes the UHE component. The angular extension of the J1837EXT component is about 0.5 degrees. The observed GeV-TeV SED for J1837EXT can be well explained by a hadronic model with an exponential cutoff power-law spectral (ECPL) index of ∼ 2.1 and a cutoff energy of 66 TeV. Our findings suggest that the emissions from J1837EXT most likely originate from the interaction of particles accelerated by the supernova remnant (SNR) embedded in the young massive star cluster RSGC1 with ambient gas. However, a scenario where cosmic rays (CRs) are accelerated by the stellar winds of the young star-forming region W42, and then transported to interact with clouds to produce in the observed region, cannot be completely ruled out.

nodes.name: From sensing to clinical translation: advances and challenges in wearable cuffless blood pressure monitoring
nodes.venue: Sensor Review
nodes.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to systematically synthesize state-of-the-art advancements in wearable cuffless blood pressure (BP) monitoring technologies, critically examining the sensing hardware, estimation algorithms and calibration strategies and identifying the core barriers that impede the translation from laboratory prototypes to clinically reliable cardiovascular monitoring systems. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a comprehensive literature review approach, systematically analyzing emerging sensing modalities – including optoelectronic (PPG), mechanoelectric (triboelectric, piezoelectric, piezoresistive), ultrasonic and multimodal fusion systems – alongside the evolutionary trajectory of BP estimation techniques, from mechanism-driven models (PTT/PWV) through data-driven deep learning to the emerging physics-informed artificial intelligence paradigm. Clinical validation frameworks and calibration strategies are also critically assessed. Findings The review reveals that while significant progress has been made in sensor sensitivity, signal processing and algorithmic accuracy, several critical barriers persist before widespread clinical adoption. These include motion-induced signal degradation, limited cross-population generalizability of algorithms, the absence of standardized validation protocols for cuffless devices and calibration drift over time. Physics-informed AI emerges as a promising paradigm for improving robustness, interpretability and generalization by embedding hemodynamic constraints into data-driven models. Research limitations/implications As a review paper, the findings are based on published literature rather than original experimental data. Future research should focus on adaptive calibration frameworks, rigorous multi-scenario validation aligned with ESH 2023 recommendations and hardware-software co-design approaches. Practical implications The review provides actionable guidance for researchers, clinicians, and device developers by identifying key technological bottlenecks and outlining future directions, including endogenous autonomous calibration benchmarks and multimodal sensing integration, to accelerate the development of clinically viable wearable BP monitoring systems. Originality/value This paper uniquely bridges the gap between sensing hardware and clinical requirements by providing an integrated analysis across the full technology chain – from sensors to algorithms to clinical translation. It highlights physics-informed AI as a critical emerging direction and proposes a forward-looking framework for all-scenario adaptive dynamic calibration, offering a comprehensive roadmap for the field.

nodes.name: Construction cost prediction using TabPFN-based stacking model with SHAP analysis
nodes.venue: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
nodes.abstract: Purpose Construction cost prediction is essential for improving budget management, risk reduction, and resource allocation in the construction industry. This study aims to enhance prediction accuracy by proposing a stacked ensemble model that integrates Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN), CatBoost, and Gradient Boosted Decision Trees “GBDT” while incorporating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) value analysis for interpretability. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a two-layer stacking ensemble model using San Francisco building permit data, where Estimated Cost denotes the permit-declared pre-commencement cost estimate. TabPFN and CatBoost are used as first-layer base learners, and their out-of-fold predictions are combined with original project features as inputs to a second-layer GBDT meta-learner. Model performance is evaluated using 10 independent random train-test splits. In each run, the training set is used for leakage-controlled 5-fold cross-validation and model tuning, and final performance is reported as the mean ± standard deviation across the 10 runs. RMSE, MAE, and MAPE were employed in comparison with baseline models, and SHAP values are applied for model interpretation. Findings The proposed TabPFN + CatBoost-GBDT model achieves robust performance, with a MAPE of 1.89% for recorded permit-estimated costs. This indicates close alignment between predicted values and declared pre-commencement cost estimates, although the results should not be interpreted as final realized construction costs. Additional diagnostics show that high-cost projects remain more difficult to predict. The low prediction error indicates that the model can provide more reliable pre-commencement cost estimates, which may assist contractors in bid pricing, budget control, contingency planning, and resource allocation by reducing uncertainty in expected project expenditures. Originality/value This study extends pretrained tabular learning to construction cost prediction by integrating TabPFN, CatBoost, and GBDT in a task-specific stacking framework. It combines pretrained tabular representation, categorical feature handling, and feature-informed meta-learning. SHAP analysis is further used to explain how the final model combines first-layer predictions and original project variables, while raw feature interpretation is treated as conditional and partly indirect.

nodes.name: Vehicle-mounted LiDAR-inertial odometry localization and mapping system based on FAST-LIO2
nodes.venue: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)
nodes.abstract: To meet the rapid localization and mapping requirements of autonomous vehicles, this paper builds a vehicle-mounted LiDAR-IMU-GPS test platform on ROS2 using the FAST-LIO2 LiDAR-inertial odometry algorithm. A data preprocessing and time alignment module is designed to address timing synchronization anomalies among multi-source sensors in real-world data. Campus experiments show that the platform maintains stable localization and mapping over short distances, whereas cumulative drift becomes significant over long-distance operation. The proposed preprocessing and time alignment module, together with a constrained test environment, effectively improves localization accuracy and mapping quality.

Unsupervised Marine Radar Oil Spill Detection via an Autoencoder–IAEA Synergistic Framework
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Marine oil spill accidents pose serious threats to marine ecosystems and coastal economic development. X-band marine radar provides an effective means for nearshore oil spill monitoring, yet accurate oil film segmentation remains challenging because of grayscale overlap between oil films and sea clutter, range-dependent echo attenuation, and noise interference. To address these challenges, an unsupervised oil spill detection method integrating HBA-AE ROI extraction with IAEA fine segmentation is proposed. In the coarse detection stage, an autoencoder (AE) maps pixel grayscale intensity, local mean, and local standard deviation into a compact two-dimensional latent space. The AE-derived latent representation is further optimized by HBA to enhance oil film–sea clutter separability, after which K-Means clustering identifies candidate oil spill ROIs. In the subsequent fine segmentation stage, the extracted ROI constrains the search domain, while the Improved Alpha Evolution Algorithm (IAEA) maximizes the three-class Otsu between-class variance to determine the optimal dual thresholds for oil film delineation. Experiments using X-band marine radar data collected during the Dalian 7·16 oil spill accident were conducted against seven representative methods. The proposed framework achieved a Precision of 97.20%, an F1-score of 86.60%, and an IoU of 76.40%, demonstrating superior oil film segmentation accuracy and effective false-alarm suppression under complex sea-clutter conditions. It also maintained a favorable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, demonstrating its potential for marine oil spill monitoring under the investigated radar observation conditions.

nodes.name: Toward trustworthy IoMT healthcare: federated learning and verifiable blockchain for secure edge-driven EHR systems
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract The advent of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has made it necessary to exchange electronic health records (EHRs) across distributed healthcare entities in a manner that ensures their authentication and preserves patients’ privacy. This paper proposes the Federated and Blockchain-enabled Electronic Health Record (FBEHR) framework whose major contribution is the Improved Universal Designated Verifier Signature Proof (IUDVSP). Different from all other pairing-based UDVSP schemes, the suggested solution uses elliptic curve arithmetic compatible with ECDSA to ensure signer authenticity, designated-verifier privacy, and verification control without employing bilinear pairings. According to our experiments in the × 86 edge-server environment, IUDVSP takes 0.22 ms to generate signatures and 0.28 ms to verify them. While these results are below 2-4 ms that we take as the cost of one pairing operation in the adopted reference architecture, they are not the result of a direct same-platform performance comparison of the suggested algorithm with a complete pairing-based UDVSP protocol. The framework also features blockchain-based EHR registration, validation, access, revocation and federated ANN-LSTM-based malicious-user detection. In an internal evaluation of the suggested system, activation of edge processing results in the mean registration and validation latency reduction from 9.87 to 3.59 s which corresponds to the 62.76% latency improvement relative to the same framework but without edge processing. Performance of the FBEHR relative to existing baselines is similar; thus, the primary benefit of FBEHR is its pairing-free designated-verifier security, not latency improvement over those systems. An estimation of the total cost of ownership for a month-long period of FBEHR deployment gives us USD 1850 for the considered FBEHR architecture and USD 12,500 for the same architecture but centralized. This difference of 85.2% is calculated based on a model and is not the experimental performance cost reduction.

nodes.name: Three-Dimensional Source Localization of Natural Gas Leakage Using an Experimentally-Calibrated Gaussian Plume Model and Enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract To address the challenges associated with the three-dimensional source localization of surface natural gas micro-leakages, this study proposes a novel three-dimensional localization method that integrates an experimentally-calibrated Gaussian plume model with an enhanced particle swarm optimization algorithm (EGPM-EPSO). The proposed method was evaluated systematically through controlled test-rig experiments, followed by preliminary field demonstration. A well-conditioned experimental platform was first designed to quantitatively characterize the spatial distribution of the leaked gas concentrations using tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy. A plume rise impact factor was introduced to describe the coupled effect of the leakage rate and wind speed, based on which an exponential saturation model for the plume rise height was developed. An experimentally-calibrated Gaussian plume model (EGPM) was established by further deriving the lateral and vertical diffusion parameters using experimental data. Compared to traditional models, the EGPM substantially improved the concentration prediction accuracy, reducing the average relative error to 1.65%. The EGPM was then integrated with an enhanced particle swarm optimization algorithm incorporating several strategic improvements, achieving a mean localization error of 0.0084 m on the experimental platform. Additionally, field testing for natural gas leakage was conducted via a vehicle-mounted mobile monitoring system. The results indicate that the proposed three-dimensional localization method can accurately identify the leakage source with a total localization error of 3.1 m. The measurement-driven inversion framework establishes a robust foundation for the safety monitoring and emergency response of gas pipeline leakages.

nodes.name: The capability of very high-resolution satellite imagery for plot-level early wheat stem rust disease detection, monitoring, and phenotyping in Ethiopia
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract Very high‑resolution satellites (VHRS) have potential for early crop disease detection and enhanced food security. The capability of multispectral SkySat and Pleiades‑Neo imagery for early-stage detection and monitoring was assessed for wheat stem rust (SR) at the plot level. In randomized trials with contrasting fungicide and irrigation treatments, six bread wheat varieties with differing SR susceptibility were monitored using VHRS. 113 multispectral features were evaluated for their association with SR progression and associated yield loss. Several features demonstrated moderate to strong correlations with SR disease levels. Across early stages (healthy, mildly diseased, and moderately diseased), spectral sensitivity was dominated by Blue (B)‑based features, with Red-Blue (R-B) and Green-Blue (G-B) two-band features at mildly and moderately diseased levels, respectively. During late stages (severely diseased and fully diseased), spectral sensitivity was driven by R-based features (e.g., R-B, R-G on both sensors) and by Deep Blue (DB), Red-Edge-DB (RE-DB), and R-DB combinations on Pleiades‑Neo. Early-stage SR detection under moderate disease pressure was possible using ratio (RSI) and normalized difference (NDSI) spectral indices with B-G combinations. SkySat features such as RSI(NIR,B), RSI(R,B), and RSI(G,B) were consistently associated with SR across multiple disease scenarios, trials, and disease metrics. This work delivers the first VHRS-based SR detection at the plot scale and provides a foundation for future investigations into SR monitoring across larger spatial scales.

nodes.name: Task-routed hierarchical patch memories for industrial anomaly detection and localization
nodes.venue: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)
nodes.abstract: Industrial anomaly inspection must detect and localize defects, but patch-memory methods use one feature hierarchy for both outputs. This creates a task-dependent hierarchy conflict: deeper features aid image discrimination, whereas pixel localization requires spatial evidence weakened by resizing and aggregation. We propose TRHM-PatchCore, a normal only task-routed hierarchical patch-memory framework. At inference, one shared frozen pretrained WideResNet-50-2 extracts layers 1-3 once for two task-specific memory heads. Global aggregates layers 2 and 3, uses all extracted descriptors before 10% coreset selection, and supplies the image anomaly score. Detail aggregates layers 1 and 2, deterministically samples 2,048 descriptors per normal image before the same coreset procedure and supplies the pixel anomaly map. The final system applies fixed task routing rather than score fusion. On all eight MVTec AD 2 TESTpub categories, Global obtains macro-Image AUROC/AP of 0.7520/0.8350, whereas Detail raises macro AU-PRO@0.05 from 0.3681 to 0.4230 and AU-PRO@0.30 from 0.6096 to 0.6905. Across all eight categories, Detail retains macro-AU-PRO gains of +0.0477/+0.0714 under matched descriptor count, +0.0539/+0.0746 under matched storage, and +0.0540/+0.0769 under a matched nearest-neighbor search proxy at FPR limits 0.05/0.30, respectively. Across five matched-budget coreset seeds, the Detail-minus-Coarse AU-PRO gains are +0.0468 (95% CI 0.0437-0.0499) and +0.0692 (0.0667-0.0717) at FPR limits 0.05 and 0.30. On untouched Magnetic Tile, it matches standard PatchCore image metrics; AU-PRO@0.05/@0.30 is 0.5724/0.8124 versus 0.5604/0.7960.

nodes.name: Smart Black–Box Architecture For Autonomous Accident Detection And Geo location
nodes.venue: Journal of Electrical Engineering and Automation
nodes.abstract: This research work proposes an intelligent black-box design framework for accident prevention, detection and geolocation through the integration of heterogeneous sensing and communication devices into the embedded ATmega platform. The proposed system combines an MQ3 alcohol sensing device, seat belt sensor, eye blink sensor, DHT11 temperature sensor, ultrasonic sensor, and ADXL335 accelerometer. Condition based control actions are employed to stop the prototype engine if the rider consumed alcohol, warning generation for long eye closure and high temperature, and reduces prototype engine speed when close vehicle proximity is detected. In case of an accident, the accelerator triggers the emergency response process by sending the user’s location acquisition using GPS coordinates and transmission of latitude and longitude along with the Google Maps link to emergency contacts through GSM. Stepper motor helps to illustrate the control responses. The presented prototype implementation through serial monitor observations and emergency message transmission confirms the sensing, decision-making, accident detection, location acquisition, and notification process proves the effectiveness of the proposed design in real-time scenarios.

nodes.name: Journal of Electrical Engineering and Automation
STELLAR: Large Language Model Enhanced Spatiotemporal Semantic Fusion for Urban Next POI Recommendation
nodes.venue: Symmetry
nodes.abstract: Urban next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation is fundamental to location-based services, yet accurate prediction remains challenging because user trajectories are sparse, semantically incomplete, and tightly constrained by time and geography. Recent graph and Transformer models capture transition regularities, while language model-based recommenders introduce textual knowledge, but these two lines of work remain weakly coupled: semantic priors may be plausible in language space yet infeasible under a user’s actual mobility state, and purely behavioral encoders fail to infer latent intent when observations are scarce. We introduce STELLAR, a unified state transition framework that treats language knowledge as a calibrated prior rather than an independent prediction branch. STELLAR first induces semantic mobility priors from structured trajectory descriptions, then projects them into a shared transition state and learns a feasibility gate conditioned on spatial reachability, temporal rhythm, and both short- and long-term behavioral context. A transition memory subsequently propagates this calibrated state to candidate POIs, allowing semantic evidence to influence prediction only when it is consistent with executable mobility. This design directly addresses semantic-behavioral misalignment and avoids ad hoc late fusion. Across three public check-in benchmarks, STELLAR consistently outperforms both purely behavioral and language-augmented baselines in ranking accuracy, robustness to corrupted trajectories, and cold-start generalization.

nodes.name: Rs-PromptIR: spatially-adaptive sparse prompting with orthogonal regularization for all-in-one image restoration
nodes.venue: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)
nodes.abstract: All-in-one image restoration aims to recover high-quality images from various degradation types using a single unified model. While recently proposed prompt-based methods (e.g., PromptIR[2]) have demonstrated significant potential, they predominantly rely on global descriptors for prompt weight generation. This approach overlooks the spatially localized heterogeneity of degradation—such as the co-occurrence of rain streaks and haze in disparate regions of the same image—thereby leading to redundancy in prompt information. In this paper, we propose RS-PromptIR, an enhanced framework featuring a Regional Sparse Multi-Head Cross-Attention (RSM) Block. Unlike prior works, our RSM-Block performs regional routing by partitioning the feature map into grids and utilizing multi-head cross-attention to match local queries with a learnable prompt pool. Furthermore, we introduce a Top-k sparsity mechanism to select the most relevant prompt experts, effectively reducing inter-task interference. To ensure the diversity and representational capacity of the prompt pool, a Soft Orthogonal Loss is formulated to minimize redundancy among prompt experts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RS-PromptIR attains state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating particularly remarkable efficacy in complex scenarios characterized by spatially localized heterogeneous degradations.

nodes.name: Research on a nut measurement system based on binocular stereo vision
nodes.venue: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)
nodes.abstract: Aiming at the challenging problem of high-precision automated detection for the spatial coordinates and inner diameter dimensions of nuts in complex industrial field environments, this paper proposes a measurement system scheme based on a binocular stereo camera. The system constructs a complete closed-loop workflow ranging from camera calibration and anti-noise preprocessing to robust feature extraction and 3D dimensional calculation. First, the Zhang Zhengyou calibration method is utilized to achieve precise calibration of the binocular system. Second, Canny edge detection and Hough transform algorithms are employed to achieve high-precision extraction of nut edge features in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments. Finally, based on the principle of stereo parallax, the 3D point cloud data of the nut is reconstructed to calculate its spatial pose and physical inner diameter dimensions. Experimental results indicate that the system can effectively adapt to interference in industrial settings, achieving non-contact precision measurement of key nut parameters. This provides reliable technical support for quality control in automated assembly lines.

nodes.name: Remote sensing image dehazing based on frequency-domain feature-guided self-attention mechanism
nodes.venue: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)
nodes.abstract: Existing remote sensing image dehazing methods are restricted by narrow receptive fields of spatial convolution operators, which fail to model long-range contextual dependencies and recover delicate high-frequency textures. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight Frequency-Feature-Guided Stripe-Window Self-Attention Network (FFG-SANet) for remote sensing haze removal. We construct a bidirectional cross-stripe self-attention module to capture large-scale ground object context, paired with a multi-scale Fourier frequency branch to compensate missing fine textures with marginal computational burden. Comprehensive experiments across four synthetic and real hazy remote sensing benchmarks validate the independent contribution of the two core modules via split ablation studies. Compared with the competitive DehazeFormer, FFG-SANet lifts PSNR by 0.1dB while cutting parameter volume by nearly half. Supplementary inference efficiency tests further demonstrate that our network achieves lower latency and higher throughput than mainstream lightweight dehazing models. The proposed method substantially improves visual clarity and radiometric fidelity of degraded remote sensing imagery, providing reliable data support for downstream tasks including target detection, environmental monitoring, disaster assessment and refined urban planning, with promising practical deployment prospects.

nodes.name: RSDMF-DETR: A Remote Sensing Direction-aware Multi-scale Fusion Detection Transformer
nodes.venue: Engineering Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract With the expansion of wind power scale, UAV-based remote sensing technology has become an important approach for wind turbine object detection in intelligent inspection, operation and maintenance, and wind energy resource assessment. Compared with traditional manual inspections, UAV remote sensing provides advantages of non-contact operation, wide coverage, rapid acquisition, and high spatial resolution. However, wind turbine objects exhibit significant scale variations, diverse orientations, and complex backgrounds, posing challenges to feature representation, multi-scale fusion, and robust detection. To address these challenges, this paper constructs a UAV-based remote sensing dataset and proposes a Remote Sensing Direction-aware Multi-scale Fusion Detection Transformer (RSDMF-DETR), a task-oriented, stage-wise framework that integrates existing feature extraction components with two self-designed modules, Remote Spatial Direction Attention (RSDA) and Scale-Enhanced Bidirectional Channel-Spatial Attention (SE-BCSA). Specifically, the backbone adopts the existing Context-Guided Block (CGB) to jointly model local texture information and contextual semantic cues, thereby improving feature representation under complex backgrounds. The Remote Direction-Aware Encoding Network (RDEN) integrates existing GSConv and VoVGSCSP components with the proposed RSDA module to enhance feature encoding, cross-layer aggregation, and directional structural representation. Finally, the Remote Multi-scale Adaptive Fusion (RMAF) stage combines the existing DynamicScalSeq component with the proposed SE-BCSA module to enhance cross-scale feature alignment and channel-spatial feature refinement. Experimental results on the self-built UAV remote sensing dataset demonstrate that RSDMF-DETR achieves 89.5% 〖AP〗_(IoU=50) and 67.1% 〖AP〗_(IoU=50:95), representing improvements of 2.0 and 0.8 percentage points over RT-DETR-R18, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed stage-wise strategy effectively integrates contextual, directional, and multi-scale feature representations for wind turbine detection under complex remote sensing conditions. RSDMF-DETR may provide target-level information for wind farm inspection, localization, and spatial information management. Its deployment and performance on actual UAV or edge-computing platforms have not yet been experimentally validated and remain topics for future work.
